subject: Approval needed: Marketplace positioning language (AWS/GCP) + competitive claim guardrails
body:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Approval needed: Marketplace positioning language (AWS/GCP) + competitive claim guardrails

Hi Evelyn + Jordan,

We’re finalizing the AWS/GCP Marketplace listing refresh this week and need exec approval on the positioning language + competitive claim guardrails (so we don’t create compliance/legal review churn during marketplace submission).

Ask (please reply “Approved” or with edits by EOD today PT):
1) Approve the core one-liner + “why Redwood” bullets (below)
2) Approve the competitive language guardrails (what we will NOT say)

Proposed marketplace one-liner:
“Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for high-performance, reliable LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.”

Proposed proof/value bullets (listing-safe):
- Production-grade inference economics: latency + token cost controls via smart batching/caching and routing policies.
- Flexible deployment: Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem) with a consistent API and operational tooling.
- Reliability features: fallbacks across compatible model variants/regions + rollout policies (canary/A-B).
- Enterprise readiness: audit logs, encryption with KMS integrations, configurable retention controls (see security packet).

Competitive claim guardrails:
- No “best in class,” “#1,” “lowest cost,” or “faster than <vendor>” claims.
- No naming competitor products in the listing copy.
- We can reference “Redwood-verified performance profiles” and link to our benchmark methodology page (not marketplace copy).

Attachments:
- Marketplace_Positioning_CopyBlocks_v0.9.docx
- Marketplace_Copy_DoDont_v0.9.pdf

Drive links:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1pmm-positioning-copyblocks-v0-9
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1pmm-marketplace-do-dont-v0-9

If helpful, the Confluence guidelines page we’re aligning to:
confluence://sales-enablement/positioning-and-messaging/marketplace-positioning-and-copy-guidelines

Thanks,
Soojin

—
Soojin Lee
Director, Product Marketing
Redwood Inference


From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 9:28 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Marketplace positioning language (AWS/GCP) + competitive claim guardrails

Works for me.

One tweak: can we make “enterprise readiness” less feature-laundry and more buyer-outcome? Maybe:
“Enterprise controls: encryption w/ customer-managed keys (KMS), audit logs, and configurable retention to meet internal security requirements.”

Also +1 on not naming competitors.

Jordan

—
Jordan Blake
CRO, Redwood Inference


From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Marketplace positioning language (AWS/GCP) + competitive claim guardrails

+1.

Minor edit suggestion on the one-liner: remove “developer-first” (marketplace reviewers sometimes read it as marketing fluff) and keep it concrete.

Option:
“Redwood Inference is a platform for high-performance, reliable LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.”

Also, “fall back across compatible model variants/regions” reads a bit scary—can we phrase as resiliency?
“Built-in resiliency with routing + fallback policies to keep applications online.”

Camila

—
Camila Reyes
VP Marketing, Redwood Inference


From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 10:21 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Marketplace positioning language (AWS/GCP) + competitive claim guardrails

Thanks Soojin.

From legal perspective, the guardrails are the right direction.

Two notes:
1) Avoid “guarantees” unless tied to a named SLA and specific SKU/offer terms.
2) “Redwood-verified performance profiles” is ok as long as we don’t imply independent certification. Recommend we keep it as “Redwood-tested” or “Redwood benchmarked” and ensure the linked methodology page explains scope.

Otherwise, approved conceptually.

Michael

—
Michael Grant
Legal Sponsor (terms), Redwood Inference


From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 11:07 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Marketplace positioning language (AWS/GCP) + competitive claim guardrails

Thanks all—integrating edits now.

Revised (for final approval):

One-liner:
“Redwood Inference is a platform for high-performance, reliable LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.”

Bullets (updated):
- Production-grade inference economics: latency + unit cost controls via smart batching/caching and routing policies.
- Flexible deployment: Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem) with a consistent API + operational tooling.
- Built-in resiliency with routing + fallback policies to keep applications online.
- Enterprise controls: encryption with customer-managed keys (KMS integrations), audit logs, and configurable retention.

Competitive guardrails (updated):
- No superlatives or competitor call-outs.
- No cost/latency claims unless (a) we can cite the source and (b) it’s not in the marketplace listing itself.
- Use “Redwood-benchmarked” instead of “verified.”

Evelyn—can you reply with final sign-off on the revised blocks?

Soojin


From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 11:33 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Marketplace positioning language (AWS/GCP) + competitive claim guardrails

Looks good.

Small sales note: “Hosted API” is clear; for Dedicated/Private, can we add 2–3 words that map to procurement language? Buyers ask for “reserved capacity” and “VPC.”

Maybe:
“Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs)” and “Private (VPC/on-prem).”

Stephanie

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Lukas

Subject: Re: Approval needed: Marketplace positioning language (AWS/GCP) + competitive claim guardrails

Approved with the edits captured in your revised version + Stephanie’s procurement-language tweak.

Final wording approved for marketplace listings:
- “Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs)”
- “Private (VPC/on-prem)” 

Agree with the competitive guardrails and the “Redwood-benchmarked” phrasing.

Please make sure anything SLA-related stays tied to the correct SKU/offer terms and avoid implying independent certification.

Evelyn

—
Evelyn Hart
Product Executive Sponsor, Redwood Inference
